title: Third Maximum Number
summary: Given an integer array, return the third distinct highest number.
statement: Given an integer array, return the third distinct highest number. If there is no third distinct highest, return the highest number.
constraints: Rank distinct values. With fewer than three distinct values, return the maximum.
Target O(n) time with only three retained candidates.
hints: Only the three greatest distinct values can affect the answer.
Ignore retained duplicates, insert a new value, and discard the fourth largest.
Keep at most three descending unique candidates; return the third if present, otherwise the first.
Sorting at most four values is constant work. Avoid sentinel values that collide with signed-32-bit inputs.
editorial: After each item, retain the largest min(3,distinct count) values. Repetition cannot promote a discarded smaller value. This invariant supports local deduplication and constant storage. All-negative inputs and the minimum signed integer remain ordinary values, not special markers.

tests.explanation: The distinct descending values are 3, 2, 1, so the third maximum is 1.
Repeating 2 does not change its rank; the third distinct maximum is still 1.
